newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM MONITORING SITUATION IN PNG
The Federal Government is calling on the Papua New Guinean Government to resolve the revolt in PNG peacefully, as soon as possible and in accordance with the constitution.
Papua New Guinea's army and police force have revolted and called on Prime Minister Julius Chan to resign for hiring foreign mercenaries to crush the rebellion on Bougainville.
But the Defence Force Commander, Jerry Singirok, who's heading the revolt, along with the country's police commissioner, rejects any suggestions of a coup.
Brigadier-General Singirok told a local radio there's no civil disobedience, saying that occurs when the people take the law into their own hands and cause riots.
A spokesman for the Prime Minister, says the Government is following the situation very closely and with great concern.
DEMOCRATS DECRY PNG MERCENARY MOVE
The Australian Democrats say the situation in Papua New Guinea could get out of hand fast if, as has been reported, the PNG Defence Force has detained foreign mercenaries.
Papua New Guinea's Defence Force Commander has called on the Government to resign and refused to work with mercenaries brought in to help quell the rebellion on Bougainville.

Democrats Foreign Affairs Spokesperson, Vicki Bourne, says PNG Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan probably didn't take into account the loss of face hiring mercenaries would cause the Defence Force and police.
She says Sir Julius has spent an enormous amount of money on mercenaries that as far as she can see he has never spent on the Defence force or police.
COMPANY DIRECTORS EXPECT STRONG ECONOMIC PERFORMANCE
Australian company directors are expecting a strong economic performance this year.

A survey by the Australian Institute of Company Directors and the chartered accountants, KPMG Peat Marwick, has found 67 per cent of directors expect improved economic conditions over the next 12 months.
The most optimistic directors are in the construction industry, while nearly half of wholesale and retail directors are pessimistic in the light of soft customer spending.
IRAQIS ON HUNGER STRIKE PLEAD TO MEDIA TO HELP CAUSE
A letter signed by the Iraqis on a hunger strike in the Port Hedland Detention Centre calls to the media for help in their campaign for refugee status.
One of the 24 detainees who have been refused refugee status, sent a letter, addressed to media outlets, to the Independent Council for Refugee Advocacy.
In the letter, the detainees say they want to give the media more information about their situation, and ask for a journalist to visit the centre.
The Iraqis have been refusing to eat or drink for five days, claiming if they're sent home they will face the death penalty.
A lawyer from a Victorian legal firm is on the way to Port Hedland to discuss the appeal process.
LAWYER JAILED FOR GIVING CONFIDENTIAL DOCUMENTS TO BOND'S SON
A high ranking Perth lawyer has been jailed for at least six months for giving confidential prosecution documents to the son of jailed businessman Alan Bond.
Michael Thomas Crowley, aged 38, was found guilty by a jury of wrongfully disclosing the documents which related to the prosecution of Bond over the billion-dollar Bell Resources Fraud.
At the time, Crowley was a high-ranking legal officer on the Bond investigation team.
In sentencing today, District Court Judge Robert Viol said the offence was a gross breach of Crowley's duty as a lawyer and member of the investigation team.
He rejected a Defence submission that the crime was a victimless one saying the interest of the Australian community could have been affected.
He sentenced Crowley to 15 months jail, but ordered that he be released on a 10-thousand dollar good behaviour bond after six months.
DEFAMATION PROCEEDINGS BROUGHT AGAINST ALAN JONES
The New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council has begun defamation proceedings against Sydney broadcaster, Alan Jones.
The council says the statement of claim was served on Mr Jones during his programme this morning on Radio 2UE.
Action is also being taken against 2UE and Anthony Carter, a guest on Mr Jones' programme on February the 4th this year.
The defamation proceedings relate to a discussion on air about a successful native title claim by the Dunghutti people at Crescent Head, on the mid-north coast.
TALKS UNDERWAY TO END DOCTORS' DISPUTE

Private talks are underway in the New South Wales Industrial Commission aimed at resolving the doctors' dispute that's disrupting elective surgery in New South Wales hospitals. A spokesman for the State Health Department says the talks aim to provide a forum for striking medical officers to resolve their dispute with the Federal Department of Health.
Hospital doctors in the Northern Territory have joined their New South Wales colleagues in industrial action, attempting to overturn legislation limiting the issue of Medicare provider numbers.
The Public Service Association has told the Industrial Commission that doctors want to open negotiations with Health Minister Michael Wooldridge, and have him consider alternative proposals.
Spokesman Brian Jardine says the suggestions on careers and training may lead Dr Wooldridge to abandon the provider number laws.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
